items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request updates the existing PR rather than opening a new one. The description is precise about three properties — update-not-open, refusal on person commits, and HEAD-not-branch-tip — and the diff delivers all three. The gate entry is registered, `O12`'s gate list is extended, `update_reviewable` is added to `propose.py`, `update_change` is implemented for both GitHub and GitLab adapters, the dispatch lo…[truncated]
Fallback on host error returns None and opens a new PR, potentially duplicating.
Refusal message truncates SHA to 7 characters but detection uses full SHA.
HEAD-over-branch-tip test does not actually verify the implementation mechanism.

This change adds a second-attempt update path for `/implement`: when an open CR already exists for a ticket, the run force-pushes to that branch rather than opening a new one. The performance surface is narrow — `_existing_change_for` calls `changes_for` (one network round-trip) and `_person_commits_on` calls `commits_between` (one more), both on a path that was previously a single `open_change` call. Neither call is in a loop, neither scales with anything unbounded, and the fallback-to-None beh…[truncated]

This change adds a second-attempt update path for `/implement`: when a prior run already opened a pull request for a ticket, the next run force-pushes to the existing branch rather than opening a new one. The human-commit safety check (trailer-based, no heuristics) and the refusal-before-push ordering are the right shape for this problem. I checked the trust boundary on `changes_for` and `commits_between`, the branch-scoping assertion, the force-push mechanism, and the content written into PR bo…[truncated]
PR body assembled from `body` and `trailers` is passed as a literal CLI argument to `gh pr edit --body`.
Commit SHA and subject from the SCM are interpolated into a ticket comment without any sanitisation.

This change adds `update_reviewable`, `update_change` on both SCM adapters, and the branching logic in `implement_propose` that routes a second `/implement` to the update path. The test file `test_update_existing_change.py` is new and exercises the four cases named in GATE-REVIEW-8: update when CR exists, refusal on person commits, no-CR fallthrough, and HEAD-not-branch-tip ordering. I checked what each test asserts against what the production code does, and looked at the impact list for coverag…[truncated]
HEAD-over-tip test asserts absence of a key that the production code never sets, making it vacuously true.
`test_two_open_crs_uses_the_one_resolved_through` does not assert which CR is named in the ticket comment.
No test covers the `_existing_change_for` error-handling path (RuntimeError/OSError falls through to open).
